about: Formal readings of the v2 outside benchmark (stripped.jsonl), reader pass A1, made blind: without any checker output and without the expected values. Same format as benchmark/outside/dev_readings.json, one entry per item in stripped.jsonl order, except: no `actual` and no `score` (nothing was run), and the specs the readings name are not written yet: each `spec` is a path relative to benchmark/ under outside_v2/specs/, and its draft (as the reader would write it, from the item's `scheme` field) is in `specs` below, for phase B to write and check. Scheme claims take their parameters from the spec's `claims`; reconstruction claims from the component's `params`. Reasons are from the taxonomy in benchmark/outside/README.md, primary first.

readings.reading: at a first-order critical point (v' = 0, v'' != 0) and with eps = 0, the WENO-Z scheme is not fifth order: reconstruction_order_p for p = 5 fails, as for classical WENO; the second clause (no relevant influence in problems with shocks) is a numerical observation

(12) fails, which need not lower the order. Critical point of order n_cp = 1 (the source's 'v'(x_i) = 0'); the order measured on the flux difference (h_{i+1/2} - h_{i-1/2})/dx, the scheme's spatial operator (form point is the other choice); eps = 0, the item's hypothesis. The shock clause is left unformalised

readings.reading: the scalar semi-discrete KT scheme with minmod-like slopes (4.9), 1 <= theta <= 2, is TVD in time; instance: f(u) = u, theta = 1 and theta = 2, and its forward-Euler step is TVD on a CFL range [0, 1/4], which implies the semi-discrete TVD property
readings.narrowing: the theorem covers every slope satisfying the clipping condition (4.6); we take the family the sentence names ('e.g., the family of minmod-like limiters'), at its two end points theta = 1 and theta = 2 (other reading, not taken: the whole class (4.6), which would be scheme-class); scalar flux narrowed to linear advection f(u) = u, so the local speed is 1 and the flux is u^-_{j+1/2}; the semi-discrete (time-continuous) TVD property is reached through forward Euler: if u + dt L(u) is TVD for every dt/dx in [0, c] with c > 0, then d/dt TV(u(t)) <= 0 along the ODE (TV is Lipschitz), so the named claim is sufficient, not the same; c = 1/4 is our choice, any positive c would do

formalization.bridge: forward-Euler TVD on [0, 1/4] implies TV(u(t)) non-increasing for the semi-discrete ODE system (one Euler step of size dt changes u by dt L(u) + o(dt))

readings.reading: Theorem 4.1: (i) A is an invariant domain and (ii) U_i^{n+1} lies in every convex invariant set containing the values of the stencil of i; instance: each new value lies between the min and max of its stencil for nu in [0, 1/2]
readings.narrowing: narrowed to an instance: scalar linear advection f(u) = a u, a = 1 (a 1x1 hyperbolic system; f is free data of the method), one space dimension, continuous P1 elements on a uniform mesh, forward Euler; there the method is the upwind scheme (spec name gives the reduction), every interval is a convex invariant set, and the CFL condition (4.5) is nu = a dt/dx <= 1/2 (h = dx, mu = 1/2, theta_min = 1, Theorem 4.1's mesh quantities). For a scalar law the convex invariant sets are intervals, so (ii) is the local maximum principle over I(S_i) = {i-1, i, i+1}, and (i) follows from (ii); if the checker's stencil is the scheme's own {i-1, i}, its claim is stronger, hence still sufficient

formalization.bridge: (ii) for every interval B containing the stencil values is min(stencil) <= U_i^{n+1} <= max(stencil); (i) is the case B = A

gp-p1-1d-advection.json.name: Guermond-Popov first-order scheme (3.5)-(3.6) with viscosity (3.13), continuous P1 elements on a uniform 1D mesh (lumped mass m_i = dx, c_{i,i+-1} = +-1/2, c_ii = 0), f(u) = a u with a = 1, so lambda_max = |a| = 1 and d_{i,i+-1} = |a| ||c|| = 1/2, d_ii = -1; forward Euler: U_i^{n+1} = U_i - lam (a (U_{i+1} - U_{i-1})/2 - (1/2)(U_{i+1} - 2 U_i + U_{i-1})), the upwind scheme. CFL (4.5) in this setting: h = dx, mu_min = mu_max = 1/2 (1/(d+1), d = 1), theta_min = 1/(n_sh - 1) = 1, so 2 tau lambda_max mu_max/(h mu_min theta_min) = 2 nu <= 1, nu in [0, 1/2]

kt-semidiscrete-minmod-theta1-advection..name: Kurganov-Tadmor semi-discrete scheme (4.2)-(4.5), scalar f(u) = a u with a = 1, local speed (4.10) a_{j+1/2} = |a| = 1, so H_{j+1/2} = u^-_{j+1/2} = u_j + (dx/2)(u_x)_j; minmod-like slopes (4.9) with theta = 1: dx (u_x)_j = minmod(theta (u_j - u_{j-1}), (u_{j+1} - u_{j-1})/2, theta (u_{j+1} - u_j)), the three-argument minmod written as minmod(a, minmod(b, c)); the forward-Euler step of the ODE system

chen-shu-godunov-burgers.json.name: Godunov flux (3.38) with the exact (entropy) Riemann solution, scalar instance: Burgers' equation f(u) = u^2/2, for which the Godunov flux is max(f(max(uL, 0)), f(min(uR, 0))); entropy U = u^2/2

chen-shu-hll-rusanov-burgers.json.name: HLL flux (3.41) with lambda_L = -s, lambda_R = s, s = max(|uL|, |uR|) (the local Lax-Friedrichs case the source names), scalar instance: Burgers' equation f(u) = u^2/2; s >= |f'(u)| on [uL, uR], so lambda_L is not larger than the leftmost and lambda_R not smaller than the rightmost true wave speed; (3.41) gives (f_L + f_R)/2 - s (uR - uL)/2 (and f_L = 0 when s = 0); entropy U = u^2/2

barsukow-upwind-advection.json.name: Upwind method (6.37) for q_t + c q_x = 0, branch c >= 0, with c = 1: q_i^{n+1} = q_i - nu (q_i - q_{i-1})

barsukow-modified-lf-burgers.json.name: Modified Lax-Friedrichs (9.3) as printed in Theorem 9.2, q_i^{n+1} = (q_{i-1} + 2 q_i + q_{i+1})/4 - lam (f(q_{i+1}) - f(q_{i-1}))/2, written as an update (not in flux form), scalar instance f(u) = u^2/2

barsukow-lax-wendroff-advection.json.name: Lax-Wendroff (10.1) for q_t + c q_x = 0 with c = 1: q^{n+1} = q_i - nu (q_{i+1} - q_{i-1})/2 + nu^2 (q_{i+1} - 2 q_i + q_{i-1})/2

barsukow-beam-warming-advection.json.name: Beam-Warming (10.2), branch c > 0, with c = 1: q^{n+1} = q_i - nu (3 q_i - 4 q_{i-1} + q_{i-2})/2 + nu^2 (q_i - 2 q_{i-1} + q_{i-2})/2

barsukow-slope-fromm-advection.json.name: Slope method (10.16), branch c > 0, with c = 1 and the central slope s_i = (q_{i+1} - q_{i-1})/(2 dx) (= (d_x q)(x_i) + O(dx^2), so the theorem's condition holds): q^{n+1} = q_i - nu (q_i - q_{i-1}) - (nu (1 - nu)/2) dx (s_i - s_{i-1})
